name: Blake Pouch Cyst

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Blake Pouch Cyst

criteria.description: Presence of a retrocerebellar cyst communicating with the fourth ventricle on MRI
Demonstration of communication between the cyst and the fourth ventricle without cerebellar vermis hypoplasia
Normal or near-normal cerebellar vermis size and morphology on imaging
Presence of hydrocephalus or signs of increased intracranial pressure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a retrocerebellar cyst communicating with the fourth ventricle and normal cerebellar vermis morphology on MRI
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological; clinical symptoms may vary and are not always present.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Retrocerebellar cyst communicating with the fourth ventricle
searchTerms: cyst near cerebellum connected to ventricle
retrocerebellar cyst communicating with brain fluid space
posterior fossa cyst linked to fourth ventricle

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal cerebellar vermis morphology despite cyst presence
searchTerms: normal cerebellar midline structure despite cyst
intact cerebellar vermis with cyst present

common.symptomName: Hydrocephalus due to cerebrospinal fluid obstruction
searchTerms: brain swelling due to CSF obstruction

common.symptomName: Headache secondary to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain due to increased intracranial pressure

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to intracranial hypertension
searchTerms: nausea caused by increased head pressure
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

imaging: MRI showing retrocerebellar cyst communicating with the fourth ventricle
Normal cerebellar vermis morphology on MRI
Signs of hydrocephalus on brain imaging
other: Clinical signs of increased intracranial pressure such as bulging fontanelle in infants

distinguishingFeatures: Hypoplasia or agenesis of the cerebellar vermis
Enlarged fourth ventricle without direct communication with cyst
No communication with the fourth ventricle

redFlags: Rapidly increasing head circumference in infants
Signs of raised intracranial pressure (vomiting, lethargy)
Neurological deterioration or new onset seizures
references: Alvarez H, et al. Blake pouch cyst: clinical and radiological features. Childs Nerv Syst. 2017.
